item.description: Christmas is just under two months away, but College Football Christmas may come in Week 10. After the first 2026 CFP rankings on Tuesday, seven Saturday matchups now feature both teams ranked in the current Top 25. It's clear the committee is going to let this weekend solve some of the ranking scenarios, making the games that much more important and exciting. With some marquee matchups and a full slate of other games, here are our Week 10 players to watch. New Mexico safety Austin Brawley New Mexico at Nevada (Friday, 9 p.m. ET, CBSSN/DirecTV) Brawley has four interceptions this season for the Lobos. That is tied for the sixth-most in the FBS. The safety also has back-to-back games with a pick. Nevada quarterbacks have thrown 12 interceptions already this season. The Wolf Pack have featured four different QBs under center this year, but with those numbers it doesn't matter who they trot out. Brawley should have a good chance to come down with another INT this weekend. LSU QB Sam Leavitt No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC, DirecTV) Leavitt was one of the biggest transfer portal names to watch last offseason, and that only got bigger when he landed at LSU under new head coach Lane Kiffin. It looked like a perfect match in LSU's first game with a blowout win over the Clemson Tigers. The following week, he continued his hot start, throwing for 340 yards and rushing for three touchdowns. Leavitt threw three interceptions in that game against Louisiana Tech, though, and his ball security came into question. Leavitt had varying performances over his next few games, but one constant: He threw one interception in each game. The LSU quarterback has improved significantly over his last two games. item.title: Former F1 champion Jones dies aged 80
item.description: Jones helped turn Williams into one of the major forces in F1 [Getty Images] Alan Jones, the last Australian and first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world title, has died at the age of 80. Jones raced in F1 between 1975 and 1986, winning the title in 1980 to become the first of Williams' seven world champions. Jones, who turned 80 on Monday, won 12 grands prix in his career and raced competitively in other formats until 2002. "We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released on her behalf by Motorsport Australia. "He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for." Jones started the first of his 116 F1 races in a Hesketh at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix. He won his first race for the Shadow team in Austria in 1977 before joining Williams the following year. After finishing third in the drivers' championship in 1979, he won five races in 1980 and finished on the podium in all but one of the grands prix he completed, taking the title ahead of Nelson Piquet. Jones was the second Australian to win the F1 championship, after Jack Brabham in 1959, 1960 and 1966. Jones remains the most recent Australian to triumph at the Australian Grand Prix, winning at Melbourne's Calder Park Raceway in 1980 when the race was not part of the world championship. He finished third in the drivers' standings in 1981, winning in Las Vegas for what proved to be his final race victory. He retired at the end of the season. Having appeared in one race for Arrows in 1983, Jones made a full-time comeback with new team Haas in 1985 and raced largely unsuccessfully the following year. He continued to compete in touring car and endurance races, mostly in Australia, and became a popular motorsports pundit on television in his home country. "Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way," Butler-Davis said. "Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe." Breaking new ground with Williams Jones, the Williams FW07 and Patrick Head and Frank Williams in Brazil in 1981 [Getty Images] Alan Jones' time at the very peak of F1 was short - essentially just under three years from mid-1979 to the end of 1981 - but he left a lasting impression. Jones is synonymous with the Williams team, having become their first world champion in 1980, and he formed a close, almost brotherly bond with co-founders Frank Williams and Patrick Head. Williams and Head loved Jones' pugnacious, no-nonsense approach, and between them they were the leading force in F1 for a short time, as the team first emerged at the forefront of the sport. item.title: Beckett Hammers carries her family's Venice volleyball legacy forward
item.description: There are a lot of differences between the “old” gym and the new one. When Brook Hammers played at Venice in 1994, the gym was smaller and it had no air conditioning. Head coach Brian Wheatley, now a FHSAA Hall-of-Famer, was in his first season, leading an undecorated volleyball program. “It’s amazing because my 1994 team, the first year with Wheatley, was the first year that we ever won districts and regionals,” Hammers said. “So, I don’t want to say we started the tradition, but we kind of have.” Watch state volleyball games live in NFHS Network Now, 32 years later, Beckett Hammers — Brook’s daughter — is helping steward a new phase of Venice volleyball. The Indians have won the district title 25 consecutive times and 31 overall. They have won 13 regional championships, and they’re six-time state champions. Venice will look to add to their resume when they face Horizon on Friday, Nov. 6, at 11 a.m. in a Class 6A state semifinal in Winter Haven. But outside of a bigger, air-conditioned gym, Venice looks different in other ways. Wheatley left Venice in May 2024 after 30 seasons. For the first time in the state finals, the Indians will be led by head coach Jay Lanham, who has been coaching at Venice since 2003. The Elite 11: Who are Sarasota, Manatee's top volleyball players in 2026? And in their first state finals appearance since 2022, Beckett has been pivotal this season after moving to Florida last November. The junior outside hitter, who can play anywhere, has recorded a team-high 270 kills and 340 digs, 207 assists, 27 aces and 27 blocks. “She’s the type of kid who’s going to make the play,” Lanham said. “When you think that you need a big point, and you’re waiting on that huge swing, and she goes up hard and then she tips it, finds an open area on the court. That’s just a huge stop to their momentum…she’s our leader on the court.” “Since my mom graduated from Venice, I want to honor her name,” Beckett said. Brook laughs when she describes her Venice lineage. She’s “born and raised,” but that feels like an understatement. Her sister, Lori, played for Venice and coaches the freshman team. Her dad, Larry Sandburg, coached baseball and football before becoming a long-time athletic director from 1994 to 2008. Sandburg worked at Venice for 38 years. He helped hire the coaches that have turned Venice into the sports powerhouse it is, including baseball coach Craig Faulkner and football coaches John Peacock and Nick Coleman. Sandburg also hired Wheatley. The four have a combined 16 state championships. But for most of her life, Beckett has been over 600 miles away from those ties. Beckett played at Marvin Ridge High School in North Carolina, appearing in back-to-back state championship games as an underclassman under Brook, who was the head coach. Marvin Ridge lost in 2024, but won in 2025. While Beckett was born in North Carolina and the Hammers had settled there, moving back to Venice was always being discussed. item.title: Browns CB Denzel Ward weighs in on sudden turn of events for Shedeur Sanders
item.description: [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] Browns CB Denzel Ward weighs in on sudden turn of events for Shedeur Sanders appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns have been one of the most pleasant surprises of the 2026 NFL season. Cleveland is 5-3 headed into Week 9, but they may not have QB Deshaun Watson now that he’s in concussion protocol. That could set the stage for Shedeur Sanders to take over starting duties once again. One Browns defender does not sound worried about that possibility. Browns cornerback Denzel Ward explained his next man up mentality about the quarterback position in a recent interview. “Yeah, that’s the NFL. That’s just, first thought that comes to my mind is next man up mentality always, no matter the position. So quarterback position, DB, so next man up and just got to step up once you get out there,” Ward said on Wednesday, per Camryn Justice. “Whoever’s out there, if Deshaun gets back, great. If Shedeur’s out there, great. And whoever’s out there, we’ll go out there and try to win.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter against the Steelers in Week 8. He was evaluated by the league’s Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant after the play and was cleared to return. Watson also did not show signs of a concussion on Monday after the game. However, Watson’s told Cleveland’s medical team on Tuesday morning that he experienced concussion symptoms on Monday night. Shedeur is expected to start in Week 9 and will take first-team reps at practice this week. It is technically possible to get through concussion protocol in one week and still play. That said, it is much more difficult for quarterbacks than any other position when they do not get first-team reps in practice. Sanders played surprisingly well as a rookie. He logged 1,400 passing yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games last year. Now the supporting cast in Cleveland is much improved, so he could play at an even higher level. It will be fascinating to see if Shedeur can lead the Browns to a victory this weekend. Browns at Saints kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Nov 8 from Caesars Superdome in New Orleans. item.title: Henley Anderson shines bright for Texas volleyball despite the 'ring of fire'
item.description: Texas Longhorns outside hitter Henley Anderson (22) takes the court ahead of the game against Alabama in Gregory Gym on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Despite being a freshman for Texas volleyball this season, Henley Anderson has had to maneuver a "ring of fire," according to her coach. After outside hitter Abby Vander Wal suffered an ACL injury at the end of August, Anderson has had to fill her role since the third game of the season. Jerritt Elliott recognizes just how difficult that can be for a first-year player. "When you're freshmen, the pressure and everything else you go through, it's really hard to kind of perform at a high level and it's overwhelming," Elliott said in August. Henley showed power and potential early, but she had to deal with a steep learning curve as Texas played seven top-25 teams before conference play. Plus she had to get used to being a main scoring option for the Longhorns with outside hitters Torrey Stafford and Cari Spears . Elliott kept telling her to "go be Henley Anderson" and as SEC play has gone on, the Dripping Springs product has settled in nicely. UP NEXT NO. 13 TEXAS VS. MISSOURI When/where: 7 p.m. Friday in Columbia, Mo. TV: SEC Network+. In Sunday's win over A&M , Anderson had 10 kills and hit .444 in the Longhorns' sweep, which earned her a third SEC freshman of the week accolade. Elliott said he has seen her grow in a short time. "Early in the year she was just a one-trick pony," Elliott said Sunday. "Now she's doing a lot of different things: adding tips and high-line shots, learning how to tool the block, hitting deep corner, hitting hard cross. The Carolina Panthers stand in the way of the Broncos becoming winners of five in a row. Here are three storylines I’ll be watching closely in Denver’s Week 9 matchup. Who gets the lead role in the Broncos’ backfield? Earlier this morning, I gave my thoughts on how the Broncos can beat the Panthers. My first major point was getting the run game going. The Panthers have a bottom 5 run defense in the National Football League and it’s clearly their biggest weakness as a team. I think the Broncos will try and take advantage of this. item.title: Time for Texans to put their money where their mouth is…
item.description: We’ve been hearing it over and over for the last 2 years: the Texans want to play hat-on-hat, smash-mouth football. An aggressive, “establish the run” sort of offense that the Erhardt-Perkins offensive scheme flourishes with, when done properly. Unfortunately, offensive coordinator Nick Caley and offensive line coach/run game coordinator Cole Popovich have been unable to pull this rabbit out of their (un)imaginary hat. Last year, it was easy to point the finger at the mysterious injury/illness/medical foot condition of running back Joe Mixon. To rectify this in the off-season, general manager Nick Caserio traded for former Detroit Lion RB2 David Montgomery, who was promptly injured. Now, it all seems to fall on Woody Marks and a jumbo-package of basic run plays that wouldn’t fool the local High School defense, much less an NFL one. Marks is a great runner, but not a one-man Houston Texans running back depth chart. Despite mountains of evidence to make a case that the coaching is largely to blame, both in what the coaches are teaching the players and what plays Caley is calling, head coach Demeco Ryans seems to think the players are at fault, 100%. Well, if it’s a player problem, then here’s a player solution: Update: Teams have reached out to the Ravens regarding a potential trade for RB Derrick Henry, per league source. pic.twitter.com/4B1AViI8Lo — NFL Talk (@NFL_Talk_Sports) November 4, 2026 While Derrick Henry might be 33 and nearing the end of the road, he still has plenty of gas in the tank. And, on a team with Woody Marks and C.J. Stroud, he wouldn’t have to carry the entire load like he’s currently expected to do with the Baltimore Ravens. An aging lion is still lethal and threatening. Even if only the threat of him is enough to make opposing defenses fear the run some of the time. He’s also caught 12 of 14 passes for 75 yards. All this has added 9 touchdowns to the Ravens 2026 totals. Enough to put him in 7th place in the current running back Top 10. Meaning, an aging Henry is still better than most of the running backs in the NFL. 9 more touchdowns on the Texans season moves them to 5-2, if not 6-1. While other teams, such as the New York Giants, might go hard in the paint to get Henry, the Texans are at make-or-break time for the current regime. item.title: 3 bold predictions for Michigan Football vs Michigan State
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MI - OCTOBER 26: Michigan Wolverines defensive end Josaiah Stewart (0) and the team celebrate their 24-17 victory to keep the Paul Bunyan Trophy during the Michigan Wolverines versus the Michigan State Spartans game on Saturday October 26, 2024 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This weekend, the Michigan Wolverines are trying to do something they haven’t done since Sept. 19: win back-to-back games. The Wolverines beat Western Michigan, Oklahoma and UTEP to open the season, but have gone loss, loss, win, loss, win since then. That trend needs to end this weekend against Michigan State. While last week offered some encouragement in a few areas, it was a performance that left most fans disappointed. Rutgers is as bad as it gets in the Big Ten, and despite out-gaining the Scarlet Knights by nearly 200 yards, only allowing three completions, gaining 14 more first downs and nearly doubling up in time of possession, it was a one-score game that came down to the wire. Like we’ve seen so many times this season, the Wolverines played down to their competition. They were fortunate to win, but in a rivalry game, that won’t fly. Let’s make some bold predictions for this weekend’s matchup against Michigan State. Michigan will double Michigan State’s yardage There’s no doubt about it, Michigan is more talented than Michigan State. Does that mean the Wolverines are going to win? No. Michigan is also more talented than Iowa and Minnesota, and we saw how those games went. Still, the talent advantage will play a factor. Both teams struggle offensively, as the Wolverines (second-worst in the Big Ten) and Spartans (worst) have the two worst offenses in the Big Ten. However, Michigan has a massive advantage defensively. In total defense in all of college football, Michigan is ranked No. 3 out of 138 while Michigan State is No. 64. The Wolverines have a championship level defense and are going up against an offense that is depleted and struggling. item.description: The Seattle Seahawks are 4-4, just lost by 17 points to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, yet still have a +26 point differential. Turnovers have obviously been a huge factor in three of their four defeats, but a season-long issue for Seattle’s offense and defense has been seemingly unshakeable. Neither unit is getting the job done in the red zone. Seattle’s offense is one of the worst in the red zone Seattle’s offense ranks a dismal 29th in red zone touchdown percentage, scoring just 13 TDs on 28 trips. If you look at points per red zone trip, which obviously includes field goals, Seattle still ranks 29th. For whatever reason, even though red zone performance is supposedly a high-variance statistic, the Seahawks have not once fielded a top-16 offense in points per red zone possession in the post-Russell Wilson era. This is currently the worst Seahawks offense in the red zone since 2016, when they had a mostly injured Wilson at quarterback, a heavily injured running back unit, and an offensive line that was a total horror show. While the red zone encompasses the 20-yard line and in, there’s an observation I’ve made throughout the season with Brian Fleury’s playcalling. When the Seahawks are faced with a goal-to-go situation, Fleury’s default move is to run the ball to mixed (at best) results. I’m not joking: 12 runs to 1 pass. The pass was a touchdown to Cooper Kupp in the hurry-up offense against the Washington Commanders, by the way. I present to you every Seahawks goal-to-go play on 1st down this season, with the exception of a kneeldown against the Chargers. The Seahawks are the only team in the NFL with a 1st down run rate above 90% in goal-to-go situations. pic.twitter.com/ciZqYtv2TH — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 5, 2026 No other team (at least using Stathead play-by-play data ) is this run-heavy on first-and-goal than Seattle. Only the New York Giants and Cleveland Browns have thrown it once on first-and-goal. Last season, the Seahawks had a pass-run ratio of 14:19 on first-and-goal, and while the red zone offense was also lackluster under Klint Kubiak, they were not extraordinarily predictable. The first-and-goal runs are not the main reason Seattle is a poor red zone offense, but it’s certainly a factor. We’ve seen very little play-action in the red zone on any down, and the Seahawks roster generally lacks a true “go up and get it” receiving target. item.description: With no shortage of controversy in the build-up , WWE is moving forward with its annual Crown Jewel event this Saturday in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Featuring two champion vs. champion clashes, a last man standing match and a tag-team title bout, Crown Jewel has the potential to shake things up just weeks before Survivor Series: WarGames — and that isn't even factoring in both Money in the Bank briefcases, which are still waiting to be cashed in. As usual, to get you ready for the PLE, Uncrowned's Horsemen are here to answer several key questions and offer their predictions for the Saturday matinee. Let's ride! WWE appears determined to move forward with its Saudi plans, regardless of tensions within the region. ASSOCIATED PRESS 1. Sum up your thoughts on WWE's decision to keep Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. Does it impact your excitement or anticipation for the event? Robert Jackman: Where to start? I think this is a much more controversial decision than the call WWE made to run the original Crown Jewel in the wake of Jamal Khashoggi's killing back in 2018. Back then, WWE was defying what looked like a growing international boycott campaign. But as distasteful as it might have been to jet to Riyadh after a state-sanctioned killing of a dissident, Vince McMahon's WWE wasn't putting the whole company in the middle of an active warzone or defying any official travel advisories. As shocking as it is, this is exactly the sort of risk I had in mind when WWE made the big call to ramp up its Saudi partnership at the beginning of last year. Getting three times (at least) the revenue for your stadium shows without having to depend on pesky ticket sales sounds great on the face of it. But when you're taking a massive chunk of your event revenue from a single buyer, one that just happens to be an absolute monarchy in one of the world's least stable regions, it looks very different. Does it dampen my excitement for Saturday's show? I mean, this is the Crown Jewel championship we're talking about here … the champion of champions. The prize position on the WWE podium. How could I not be excited for that, right? Sorry, just practicing my corporate spiel in case I ever get recruited by TKO to the dark side. Drake Riggs: It's stupid and unnecessary, yet entirely unsurprising. I haven't wasted too much energy on this whole debacle because WWE has been treading water for so long. But it's just annoying, and you hope for everyone's safety above all else. On October 15, they fired pitching coach Alon Leichman after just a single year with the team. This past Monday, they hired Ethan Katz as his replacement . On the surface this all seems pretty simple: Leichman, in his first season as a head pitching coach, oversaw a pitching staff that had the worst ERA, the second-worst FIP, and the fifth-worst fWAR in all of MLB. item.description: Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for SiriusXM Adam Silver might be looking at trimming NBA games to 40 minutes, but Stephen A. Smith has other ideas. With Anthony Edwards and Tyrese Haliburton already missing chunks of time, the league’s health problem is front and center once again. It’s got Adam Silver seriously kicking around the idea of cutting games down to 40 minutes, similar to international ball. The thinking is straightforward, with less floor time means less wear and tear, and fewer stars potentially out on the sidelines. But shaving eight minutes off the clock hasn’t sat well with everyone, resulting in a huge pushback over whether trimming court time actually fixes player durability or just messes with the integrity of the game. Stephen A. Smith wants to eliminate back-to-backs in the NBA Stephen A. Smith wasn’t buying Adam Silver’s 40-minute pitch for a second, with the preference to reduce the amount of back-to-back games instead in the NBA . He said, on his YouTube channel : “I think the priority should be eliminating as many back-to-back games as possible.” NBA teams still face an average of 14.2 back-to-backs during the 2026–27 season, with some playing as many as 16. However, the league has eliminated four-games-in-five-nights stretches from the regular-season schedule. Teams also cannot simply rest their biggest stars whenever they choose. Under the NBA’s Player Participation Policy, teams generally cannot sit two designated star players in the same game without an approved exception. Nationally televised games also receive special protection, with stars generally expected to be available. Exceptions exist for injuries, personal circumstances and approved rest restrictions based on age, career workload or serious injury history. No. 10 Ole Miss now hosts No. 2 Georgia in Oxford on Saturday with both teams looking for a win to solidify not only its College Football Playoff chances but to improve its place in the SEC standings. So what in the name of Auburn Jesus happened to have Alex Golesh victorious over Kirby Smart? And does Ole Miss have any way to produce the same results? The biggest number that sticks out from Auburn’s upset win is the turnover margin of +3. The Bulldogs lost a fumble and starting quarterback Gunner Stockton threw two interceptions while the Tigers didn’t register a turnover all game. This isn’t one of those rocket science concepts of the game, but extra possessions even when a team is more talented, at home, playing at night, whatever the circumstances, changes the game. There’s bad news and then there’s more bad news when it comes to making this occur again. First off, the Rebels turnover margin for the season is like the GPA of Bluto in Animal House – zero point zero. Ole Miss hasn’t had much success in generating turnovers (12 thus far) and then it gives the ball away at the exact same rate.
